## Plugin reference

- Description: Queue classification (classifyQueue) consumed by the DataView Queue tab; a reorder is the server's (reorderQueue mints the rank). Ranks seeded once on creation (newest first); a waiting task group the user filed into a section (Pinned, or one of their own — the csec id kind, registered here) is read out under it. Stable-rank global queue. Ranks seeded once on creation (newest first). A user files a conversation's task group into a section — Pinned (built in, first) or one of their own sections (conversation_sections, served as queue-sections) — or leaves it in the Queue.

## Resources

The queue's live state is one bounded resource, not a push struct:

- **`queue-ranks`** (`queueRanks`) — a `liveCollection` served from the
  extension handle (`serveCollection(queueRanks, { from: conversationsQueue })`,
  so there is no `select` map to keep in sync). The sidebar reads its `:rows`
  point sibling by the LIVE conversation id set it already tracks via
  `conversations-active.v2` (`useOptimisticResource(queueRanks, { ids }, …)`), so a
  read costs O(live) (~26 rows), never O(2,726). `seedRankJob` on
  `conversationCreated` therefore ships a single-row point delta to the tuples
  containing that id (structurally none until it enters the live set), never a
  full re-select + persist. A reorder write that lands outside the subscribed
  tuple or nets to zero still confirms via **exact-ack**: the optimistic hook
  asks for standalone `ack` frames on its tuple (nothing is declared), and the
  reorder endpoint's returned `{ watermark }` is matched against the frame's
  `ackTx` (point deltas carry no snapshot watermark, so this is what replaces
  the watermark compare). Preloaded at ONE tuple, the boot id set of
  `conversations-active.v2` (`serveCollection(…, { preloadRows: { idsOf:
  conversationsActive } })`): the sidebar's tuple is exactly that set, so its
  ranks ship in the boot snapshot and the queue settles on its first render.
  Each row carries `{ conversationId, rank, section }`. The section rides the rank
  row rather than a resource of its own because it is plain user-set state: nothing
  recomputes it as conversations change status. `queue-ranks` deliberately has NO
  `dependsOn` conversations (point routing gives that structurally).

The sidebar (`data-view/plugins/queue/web/components/use-queue-rows.ts`) wraps the rows in
the client-side `QueueData { ranks }` shape so the shared `classifyQueue` stays a
pure function of plain data, and retains the last non-pending rows across
live-set re-subscriptions so a re-sub never flashes a skeleton. `applyReorder`
predicts over the LIVE rank rows only — matching the server's live-filtered
`rankAdjacentTo`.

**Retention.** `sweepGoneRanksJob` (nightly, main-only) deletes rank rows whose
conversation has been `gone` past 30 days. It is a plain scheduled `defineJob`,
not `defineRetention`: the rank side-table has no timestamp/status column of its
own, so "gone past 30 days" needs a join to `_conversations`, which the
single-table `column < cutoff` TTL shape can't express. FK CASCADE already covers
hard deletes; deleting a gone conversation's rank routes a change-feed delete only
to tuples containing that id — structurally none (it left the live set).

## Mental model

The queue is a **globally ordered, stable-rank list** of all live conversations. It answers one question: "what should I look at next?"

### Single rank, multiple sections

Every live conversation gets one fractional-index rank stored in `conversations_ext_queue.rank`. There is no per-section rank — sections are a **read-time view** partitioned by status:

| Section | Criteria |
|---|---|
| **Pinned** | Group's members are all `waiting` AND the user pinned it. Drag-and-drop reorder is available here. |
| **Queue** | Group's members are all `waiting`. Drag-and-drop reorder is available here. |
| **Working** | Group has at least one `working`/`starting` member — pinned or not. Or it supervises running work (`supervisingTaskIds`: a task it manages, at any depth, has a working/starting conversation) and none of its members waits on the user (`waitingFor`): a supervisor waiting on its agents is not waiting on you. Its rows keep their own (amber) status. |
| **Unranked** | Status is `waiting` but no rank row exists (not yet seeded or manually removed). |
| **Disconnected** | Status is `gone` but still in the active list. |
| **Done** | Recently gone conversations. |

### Task groups (clusters)

Conversations sharing the same `taskId` form a **group**. All members share the same rank — the group has a single position in the queue. The group appears as a single row represented by its most recently created member. A badge shows the member count when > 1.

- **Section assignment** is group-level: if any member is `working`/`starting`, the entire group goes to Working.
- **Shared seat**: when any group member is reordered, `reseatGroupMembers()` sets all siblings to the same new rank. A conversation joining a group takes the group's whole seat — `seatJoiningGroup()` reads rank AND section together, so it can never inherit the position without the section.

### Why the queue keeps its own `rankAdjacentTo`

Not the shared `rank/server` one, deliberately. That resolver's contract is "the
caller supplies the COMPLETE sibling set"; the queue mints against a
**status-filtered projection** on purpose — a `gone` conversation's rank row is a
tombstone awaiting the nightly sweep and must not bound a live drop. It is also a
DB reader (two indexed `LIMIT 1` seeks inside the reorder transaction, never
materializing the deck) over one flat space with no parent dimension and no
exclusion set.

### Sections (Pinned and the user's own)

`conversations_ext_queue.section` is the one spelling of where the user filed a
task group: `PINNED_SECTION` (`"pinned"`, the built-in Pinned section, fixed
first), a user section's id (`csec-…`, a row of `conversation_sections`), or
`null` (the Queue). Only the user writes it (`file`, `reorder` with `section`,
`sections/create` with a conversation, `sections/delete` returning members to
the Queue). Filing changes only which section a group is read out under — the
rank is untouched (ranks stay ONE global space; a section's order is that space
filtered), so filing back puts the group exactly where it was, and a filed group
is reorderable like any other. Every write naming a user section checks it exists
(404), so no row names a missing section; `classifyQueue` still reads an unknown
id as the Queue (a stale read).

- **The section is group-level**, like the rank: `setGroupSection` writes every
  live member of the task group. A group is ONE row in the sidebar, so a
  per-member section could split one group across two sections.
- **Working wins over every section.** A filed group that starts running shows up
  under Working and returns to its section when it finishes. Working answers
  "what is running right now"; a section answers "where do I want to keep this".

`conversation_sections` (`id` csec, `name`, `rank`, `createdAt`) is served as
`queueSections` (`queue-sections`): the whole set in rank order (`all`, `max:
200`, a user's own sections), boot-preloaded so the sidebar never paints without
it. Endpoints, each one transaction under `lockDeck`, their bodies in
`server/internal/queue-ops.ts` (executor-parametrized; `queue-ops.test.ts` drives
them on a throwaway DB): `file`, `reorder` (+ `section`), `sections/create`
(`{ name, after?, conversationId? }` → `{ id }`), `sections/rename`,
`sections/move`, `sections/delete`.

The pin began as an auto-advancing single pin (`queue_state.pinned_conversation_id`)
that tracked "your current focus" — a derived value four jobs and a validity
predicate existed to keep correct as conversations changed status. Making it
user-set deleted all of it (`validatePin`, `topWaitingByRank`, the `queue_state`
table, the `queue-pin` resource, the `pin-revalidate` / `advance-pin` jobs); the
boolean `pinned` flag then became the reserved section key (migration
`queue_section_from_pinned`).
